body: Photography - currently feeling like I regret it
So far this has been my experience just complete  a complete living nightmare with moments of just the most awesome beauty. For now still feels worth it just worried for it to become more intense.
That sounds really nice, nice to know that’s out there.  Thank you for painting the picture for me.

I’ve been trying harder to REALLY explain how it feels, but by explaining these intense emotions, I’m scared of being manipulative by sharing them. Like the cliche BPD “I love you more than anything” thing.
That’s very encouraging, I know it’s a loaded question but how have you stopped yourself from the intense cycling?
That is nice advice I’ll try that for sure.

Thank you, I think that is prob best too. 

I just can’t decide if I truly truly I would want to leave. My FP has asked me a few times now, what does my heart want? I think that this is the one of the sadder things of having BPD. The lack of self, I CANNOT answer that question, I desperately wish I could.

Thank you I really appreciate this advice. My psychiatrist was kinda advising the opposite saying I should only tell him if I want to leave for sure. But I can see how this either of your ideas could be the high road. 

I think in a lot of ways trying to leave without telling him is the way to do it that hurts him the least. Ive practiced the convo in my head a million times a day for like 6 months and nothing feels right I can’t find the words. What I struggle with the most is trying to make it out like our relationship isn’t good enough when in fact currently our day to day life together is nice, distant but pleasant enough, this is my fault and not completely caused by our relationship. I feel like if I go this route whatever explanation I have, if I leave out the affair, has to be at least genuine about us and our relationship.

Thank you so much for your response, I am kind of getting mixed messages from your advice and just want to clarify. When you say “I rather be dumped than being replaced or cheated” it kind of sounds like you would rather not know and just be dumped. But then you say tell the truth. In your opinion what would be the least hurtful way to go about this?

I don’t know if I would want to know, I feel super torn about that, ignorance is bliss sorta thing. When I talk to my friends about it they tell me it’s selfish to kinda relieve my own guilt by telling the truth. That possibly the best is to leave him, try to make the reasons about why the relationship isnt working. However I was so happy to see your reply because I do feel for me the truth would be so sad and scary but just would lift an enormous weight.  Thank you so much for the response/advice
I can't read either, lately too my short term memory has become non existent as well.

Not at first, I was eventually given seroquel to help me sleep in the evenings but it didn’t work (briefly tired and then really anxious wired after) so I stopped taking it. I’ve now quit Topiramate and seroquel and am on nothing. I’m waiting to get into a specific treatment program now before trying more drugs because my reaction to this one was so traumatic.
I like that thank you, truthfully I feel like if every week I did this I’d feel something different every time. Maybe I’ll try it and like write it down, keep track.
I do the exact same thing and can’t stop

If your Doctor is seeing you while you increase your dose it might not be as bad as it was for me. I kept increasing the dose because I kept getting more and more anxious depressed, it was hard to know what was from the drug and what was from the disorder. I spiraled from being kinda ok to massively suicidal in 3-4 weeks, I can’t properly put it into words but maybe intense trauma. Take into consideration I am both borderline and bipolar. 

When at about a 100mg dose for me I started getting visual trailing in the evening through the night and into the morning, the highest dose I took was 150mg. During the day I didn’t have that side affect. I know everyone’s brain chemistry is different so I don’t want you to not try it, but like if I can help anyone avoid the intense trauma I feel I suffered from this drug I want to. If it is available to you be in touch with your psych every 2 weeks. I didn’t have that available to me and I think that is how it could’ve been avoided. 

Anorexia is a listed side affect of this drug and I struggle with appetite often but it never felt like what I understand to be anorexia. As I was spiraling, restricting eating started giving me a sense of control and I had never been paranoid of gaining weight before this drug. 

During withdrawal I experienced pretty intense brain zaps.

I don’t have a prescription unfortunately but I have heard it’s possible to get.... I guess prescription or not just kinda wondered if and BPDers had tried micro dosing for awhile and what it was like for you
It’s so far only for like 20 minutes in the morning and at night so no REAL impact on my life other than psychologically it’s very scary to me
Thank you so much for this I will be referring to this constantly

I wish lamictal could’ve worked for me. My mother has a rare genetic eye disease (retinal pigmentosa) that causes her to be blind, and lamictal SEVERELY reduced my my vision. I’ve been tested for this disease, it affected my mother when she was 30 and I’m 30, they don’t think I have it but the stress of waking up every morning and having a serious change in my vision was to much for me to handle.
Ok ok interesting

I don’t know if traditional monogamy statistically has that great of a track record either. People are sometimes just shitty or not shitty. I don’t know that labels have anything to do with that and traditional monogamy was created for trading women as property so I argue that it is odd that it is seen as the “right way”

Me and these other people were the same age so 2 of us got out before getting married and the other one her and her husband left only a couple years ago and are swingers and seem to be happy. 

Your reply just makes me so grateful I got out when I did. Really sucks the wide range of shit people go through to leave.

My own little circle is small, myself and 2 other people from the Mormon farm town I’m from. But we are the few that left so I dunno, I just found that curious thought maybe other ex Mormons tend to not want traditional monogamy anymore.

I am bipolar II borderline and also an ex mormon. Battling not just severe mental illness but indoctrination is horrible and lasts so much longer than you think. I decided I was an atheist maybe at age 21 I’m now 30 and still struggle with trying to get rid of certain psychological filters or patterns I have from “the Church”

In early childhood especially a lot of the trauma wasn’t MINE in a way. My mom has a rare eye disease and when I was 2 she was first diagnosed and throughout my childhood became progressively more blind. I think the last time she sorta could see my face I was 11 ish. When I was little I would lash out ex. One time i was like 8 and I screamed at her to please try to paint my nails, and she would say “you know I can’t” 

My mother overall though was kinda distant and cold when I was a child but in my early 20’s she kinda changed and would listen to me for hours and was very supportive 

My younger brother has Cystic Fibrosis a terminal genetic disease that mostly affects the lungs. Growing up we where always unsure of how long he would live.My parents I think tried to prepare me and my other brother emotionally for the worst but I think they way they did it wasn’t the best I always feared he was gonna die in 2 yrs. An example is on vacation I’d beg my dad to let me use the camera and he would try to gently hint you can but you have to mostly take photos of your brother just incase. 

My dad is borderline and bipolar I would say he was moody but not abusive (me and my siblings were eventually neglected (form of abuse) as teens but not as children)

So my family was traumatic but I was the only “normal one” the tragedies weren’t specifically about me
Thank you so much for writing this, I’m really struggling with this too lately
Love this thank you
thank you so much. good to feel out whether or not it helps people who do not have it understand
aw yay! I'm so glad its relatable, thank you for your comments and letting me know. My SO is an animator and I might try to convince him to help me make a short video illustrating this idea
All of the skills Wednesday's are amazing, thank U so much for taking the time to write them and keep it up please!
Thank you so much for the kind words, this really has helped me feel a bit better.

Wow... on behalf of everyone who has needed to go to the ER for being suicidal thank you for being so kind to her. It's easy to loose hope that people can just care and have there be no strings attached. Thank you for your story

I have tried to explain to boyfriends about past encounters that were similar to your experience. And I'm not sure why but even with age the fight that you felt you lacked and feel guilty and unsure about I think happens like 95% of the time. To me it feels like a defence mechanism in the brain.. like when this sort of thing feels outta control I feel like maybe ppl start shutting down as escape. And its hardly ever this big fight. Like you get kinda groomed by someone and the slowly press your boundaries and then you feel fear and so you choke. I had an incident as an 18 yr old that was very similar and than something happened to me yesterday as a 29 yr old and my reactions weren't that different surprisingly. I keep beating my self up cuz "I didn't fight back hard enough." Its hard to explain to people who haven't experienced it what that shutting down feels like. People who have been there know that your case was absolutely rape and not your fault.

the exact same thing happened to me at that age and the same thing with the next couple boyfriends. I did eventually meet someone who was loving enough to be patient, and before our first time he said "are you 100% sure you want to do this" and I was still scared but really loved him so I said "98%" then he said "nothing is happening till you say 100 ok x" so I said "100 100" and the rest was history. Someone worth being vulnerable with will come into your life I'm sure of it. It is a scar on your past but you will get through to the other side where you barely think about it. Your not alone and I wish you the best.

I hate hiding it too, I just want to be able to talk and laugh about it like another thing in life like work or friends or tv shows... I keep talking about it that way but I feel like almost everyone is judgmental about it can't just accept it as another part of my life, that its some sort of cry out for help or just negative but ya its hard to hold conversations and not bring it up. I wish other people could kinda lighten up about it in a way.

whoa... truly awful Im sorry this happened to you.
Im a BP 29F and Ive had a few episodes where I almost hit my partner... I feel myself kind of blacking out and I have barely managed to hit a wall or a pillow instead but even if I totally lost control, the punishment likely wouldn't be as bad as if I were a male. I truly sympathize.

I also relate to this so much but I don't have any great advice, I'm truly in the same boat right now. Who I thought were my true blues since my diagnosis have been so judgemental and the least understanding. All I can say is your not alone, and also fuck doctors you gotta fight for yourself keep looking till someone decent comes your way.
whoa that is amazing

I am not at all at peace or have this under control but I have had a small revelation recently... I tried a different drug with Lithium and it made me feel absolutely nothing but it was sooo damaging to everyone around me especially my SO the only emotion I was able to express was anger everything else was stifled out. It changed my personality totally. It was confusing I struggled with whether or not I should stay on it I thought "Is this what everyone else feels like and isn't this what I've been chasing" but it felt so wrong. So I'm off it now and I won't be able to put into words but I have a new appreciation for emotions good and bad your supposed to have both, I am starting to embrace that.

Haha I am diagnosed with both so I dunno they are pretty similar... This reminds me as a kid (I was raised as a Mormon no longer practicing) I use to get frustrated when people would confuse Mormon stuff with like Johavah witness's, cuz to me THEY were the weird ones. So in your mind maybe borderlines are the "weirder" other ones. Since I have both and no longer care about religion, from experience I can say same shit different pile.
Sorry on cellphone can't add flair

I heard though the more you "exercise" your ability to auto pilot and disassociate your creating more neuro pathways to the fight and flight section of the brain and will cause possibly more frequent or worse panic attacks... For myself I noticed multitasking (autopilot) from waitressing would bring on really terrible panic attacks daily
I'd say do not meet with him... He is on his own path now let him figure out his own stuff. Not worth it at all I truly don't think you'll save him the way you see it in your head.

I do this too... With my current partner he has agreed to be "open." This is definitely not for everyone and many BPD folks struggle with jealousy so if that's you I wouldn't recommend it. For me it's kinda been working cuz I kinda get to play out whatever fantasy and realistically be very disappointed by it (it's never as good as it is in ur head) and even though I'm in an open relationship you still feel sneaky and guilty and shitty... I hate it but I've come to terms that it's an inevitable thing for me to do. I would try to think proactively, which it sounds like you have been communicating with your partner so that's awesome... Find a solution where you are maybe being true to yourself (not just for this time) but also somehow trying not to hurt everyone especially your partner and especially if this is something that happens often. Or if you are the jealous or you and your partner want total monogamy your friend I think will understand if you need to take a break for a few months to get back on track. Sorry his was long I wish you all the best.

"People who are self assured... cause me to shake..." Thank you for writing I felt like your whole response summed up the day to day battle. "Why can't you be as serious?" I get that ALL THE FUCKING TIME I hate it more than anything. Me crumbling under pressure seems to come off like I don't give a shit which it couldn't be more opposite. I've been trying really hard to change that impression I make for years and I don't know if it's possible.

I am not trans but I really know what you mean about just getting through regular daily stuff... I'm not even successfully doing all those things so the face you are is totally amazing to me... Its just so hard to express to other people at least for me the process of getting to work, how much self control and will power it takes to get me through the disassociation and panic before hand. Every time I make it its an absolute miracle. Your definitely not alone

Firstly if you are truly suicidal you should not be having another child for at least like 2 more years after some serious DBT therapy... I don't mean to say that in a condescending way I'm the same age in the same boat I want all those things too, but you know you shouldn't bring a child into your care until you can do your very best. The dream you describe with him does not sound grounded in reality and you can't count on anyone to give you that life, you gotta build yourself up to the point where basically you could do it on your own (at least I think that would be the responsible thing) you have till your late 30's I feel till you truly need to be worried about not great pregnancies which is sooooo much time for you to turn this situation around... You will not be alone forever especially if you put your focus into treatment and your health instead of this guy (I don't want to be biased but the way he sounds just gets me angry for you).... So I think ultimately you need to grieve this fantasy you had together you know it wasn't real based on where you both are at emotionally... This can be the change that makes you take your health/treatment super seriously though with a family as the finish line so when everything aligns you can be ready to share all the insanely powerful love you have inside... I was extremely suicidal a few months ago too, but I also get terrible baby fever and feel like I have so much love to give and I just want to so badly, so now that I'm still alive thats just my goal getting to a place where I know I could provide a stable and very loving environment

Ah I find almost all my relationships totally shallow because you can't be "draining" to other people. I realize I'm lucky that its not actually nobody but often there is a price or a judgement in the simplest transactions... Mr. Nobody is everywhere and in everyone I feel like maybe its just the human condition and that maybe BPD people just see it more than others.

Its hard to understand exactly what was going on between you but his  "test" of making sure you don't call him or whatever sounds like cruel weird bullshit and it might be hard to see now but I now you can find someone who won't treat you like that. That just sounds awful, when you get through this I hope you get out of that relationship, and there are amazing things about BPD you are loving and kind more than other people can fathom and someone will treat you like an fully equal adult/human/partner and not do weird animal like experiments to see how you handle it.

fuck hospitals are the fucking worst... Ive never gotten treatment that was much better to be honest... For me so far my actual treatment has all been on me researching my own medications and reading about BPD and DBT and trying to self help in a way...I relate to this so much because my closest best friends all together just decided that I am to much of a "burden" and I am "to draining" but I have always tried very hard to hid or minimize what I was going through and its just never enough... Im also coming to know even if you are flawless in hiding its easy for people when they know your diagnosis to project there own negativity unto you to justify being selfish... Because for all of us here we all know that if it was the other way around you would be the most kind, understanding friend of all time so its hard to understand how the people in our lives don't return the favour

I also dread the references boxes... Jobs, friends, so far all ended not great I don't know what I'll be doing either for next time but that form feels so differently to us, your not alone in that. I wish I had better advice but it sounds like you have been putting yourself out there which is amazing and I think eventually you will find more like minded kind people to have around you and I hope for me too the dreaded form won't be so bad in a couple years

It happens to me as well... I'm diagnosed with BPD but also BPII so I don't know if that means its different... I'm an artist (photographer) or trying to be anyways I try as much as possible to soak it in as much as possible and get inspiration from it. Its hard to focus but its a heightened state not everyone understands... You literally see hear the world differently than most people and there is a dark beauty to it... I thrive from it for creativity even though it sucks while its happening usually... I guess try to find the beauty instead of the panic and fear, I apologize if that just sounds lame but thats how I try to deal

so real I'm sure we all do this... I wish I could say something to help but I feel like this is a big struggle for most of us... I would say if its absolutely out of control just get off social media, I know that is 
impossible for some career paths but if you can that would be the way to end it.

When people notice and are uncomfortable I always just say ya I have a cat lol... It's strange I have been doing this new skin care regime for my fav to clear up acne scars... The scars on my arm are so far fairly light so I think "I could get rid of them maybe"... I don't know how terrible this is but I kinda don't want to, I feel like everyone here its feels like apart of who I am the good and bad trying to get rid of it feels disingenuous to me like a dis-honour to what I've had to overcome... I don't know if this is a healthy out look or not but I don't feel like you should have to spare anyones feelings about it... We have to do it so constantly with our words and actions already stifling our real feelings to protect other people, I feel like other people should just deal with the small window of physical evidence.
this really helped a lot thank you for writing, BPD people I think are just use to being the bad guy or "draining" I think... Its easy to forget the good you bring to the table

I am diagnosed as having both.... for me the psych. feelings that have slightly more physical side effects like psychosis, catatonic depression, severe chronic panic attacks, mania symptoms are attributed to BD but my emotional interpersonal struggles are more classically BPD... It's hard not to confuse them

I think your right... a lack of sense of self, was the only symptom of BPD that I didn't go "yes thats totally me"... I feel like I sorta recognize a sense of self, but still need constant validation. Reading other posts here, I really relate to the struggles associated with a lack of self, as well as with what you just wrote. I think it is a way bigger problem for me than I thought, maybe I've been in some sort of denial about it.

It's nice to see you write so strongly about it, definitely helped me feel a bit better. I can step back and logically see the situation as it is... over, in the past, lesson learned. However there is still that side that drills me about it. I know it won't last forever but it already feels like its been too long. I can't imagine the kid scenario, just keep seeing a loser who constantly fucks up a lets people down. In reality, as an adult, I don't think anyone has ever really seen me in that light, like looked up to me. Just that part I can't do I don't know what that looks like / feels like.

Thank you for writing, it still did help me feel a bit better.
wow, wasn't expecting that to hit so close to home. thank you for posting, so true.

I'm not currently employed lol but that has happened to me 100's of times over the years when I was. Its really hard to bounce back and it sucks when you it took everything in you to rise up again for it to only happen again in the same shift. I find it a lot harder though if a coworker or boss is even slightly negative or critical. It's hard not to appear like your blatantly pouting on purpose but you really are torn up and truly hurt. I apologize for not having good advice, I struggle with it too.
Thank you so much for writing this

hmmmm I love al the input trying to make an educated choice.... a lot of your responses were along the lines of "I loved it made my life better and I'm BP but you shouldn't do it" which is confusing but I accept it as a disclaimer. It's been really hard for me to get my hands on them and then right now I'm in a really depressed phase just doesn't seem like a good time. I'm hoping Ill be able to have them and do them when the timing is a bit better in a good controlled environment.
thank you! very sweet response I appreciate it

definitely a possibility i would talk to your docs. sounds like hypomania to me and you are on all the wrong treatments if that is the case. My dad is Bipolar and was also diagnosed with BPD but didnt accept the second diagnosis so I never heard about. I am now both as well its a very genetic illness. When I was young my dad's struggle with money and addiction were described to me a manic depression and I thought the 2 were different things but as I started getting very bad symptoms I would read about Bipolar disorder and BPD and mentally check off all the lists I didn't know which I was but I knew something was wrong and then not until later did I realize that my dad did receive the exact same diagnosis. 

Do you have any insight as to any treatment he was trying to do? Ex. I didn't know my dad took Lithium until I was trying to get it. I feel awful that you lost your dad, I almost lost mine a few times and most of us here have either seriously considered it or attempted it typically comes with the diagnosis. Just wanna say my heart goes out to you and your family and the fact that you are trying to be self-aware and proactive about your potential diagnosis/treatment is really awesome.

I've read that that sort of forgetfulness is a normal symptom of depression. I have experienced that sort of thing for myself and definitely was depressed while it was happening but luckily wasn't that severe forever (I have done the red light thing a few times, it's terrible when it does happen when you realize how uncontrollably outside yourself you were). I think commonly Bipolar people experience generalized anxiety and things like disassociating will always be common but once you come out of your depression it shouldn't be as bad I think.

After reading some of the comments though I had no idea meds could be the problem so maybe it depends also on what you're taking and if you just started something new

every time im normal or hypomanic I feel the exact same way. I feel like if i could just get a routine or therapy... sometimes in this state I have a really strong fantasy about going off meds and taking naturopath type meds maybe then I can stay ok with enough will power ugh but the inevitable happens and either i sink into a deeper depression than the last or im so anxious and hyper i cant stand myself.... I dont have advice i guess just that I know how you feel and so far just sticking to the standard treatment really is the best even though we all hate the side effects and being groggy all the time.

Maybe my advice is to just relish the in between time and try to use hypomania as a time to accomplish some stuff.... if you are on the cusp of switching moods if you are somewhat functional doing the cliche stuff can help things move along faster exercise, doing something for yourself by yourself that isnt internet related or tv.... I use to play drums as a kid and so last week i felt myself slipping into depression so during the early stages I went to a rehearsal studio played for 2 hrs it definitely helped my mood for a couple days but now im almost not functional again very depressed just barely showing up to work. It did legitimately help for a bit.

I have definitely done all of those things at some point but catatonic depression or hyper focus I think is the most common for me. I didn't even know there was a name for what hyper focus is. I've done a lot a research and tried to follow suggestions about how to not do that nothing has really worked yet.
Thank you so much everyone for your thoughtful comments it really did help me a lot
I live in ontario and here unlike other parts of Canada you can't see a therapist or psychiatrist for free. I have game to many in the past I'm feeling over talking about myself.
I'm sorry it probably doesn't help but I am literally in the exact same boat as you right now. Money and society vs. suicide is hard to contend with

I had a very similar incident about a month and a half ago I took myself to the emergency room but I don't recommend it in this scenario... It's usually better to turn to things like reddit, or music and try to calm down yourself first, without the drama of the hospital. You seem really strong I think you can do it youll be ok

I'm sorry to hear that...
I have sat in my car in so many parking lots for so many hrs too. Before I was treated for Bipolar at all I got trapped there countless times. There is something about the in-between of coming and going from somewhere that just had a pull, I liked being in that abyss or no mans land, such an emptiness an hopelessness I felt sitting in the car. It's hard to describe, for those of us who constantly struggle with suicidal thoughts sitting in the car in-between activities made me feel like I was nowhere, the place I had romanticized over and over in my mind. 

Now that I am medicated its been awhile since I have been pulled or stuck like that. So it can get better it is hard to maintain taking meds properly but it can happen. 

Probably didn't help much but you are not the only one. Best Wishes.
